s1.syndrome_frame: Acute orbital syndrome with pain, vision loss, and extraocular movement limitation
salient_findings: Diffuse limitation in extraocular movements in the left eye
Lacrimal sac abscess with postseptal fat stranding
key_facts: Several months of epiphora without prior dacryocystitis
Left-sided lacrimal sac abscess on CT
Postseptal fat stranding largely limited to the extraconal space
Acute injury to the entire orbital segment of the left optic nerve on diffusion-weighted imaging
Initial cultures isolated gram-positive cocci in chains, later identified as pan-susceptible Streptococcus pyogenes

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute orbital syndrome with pain, vision loss, and extraocular movement limitation
salient_findings: Diffuse limitation in extraocular movements in the left eye
Lacrimal sac abscess with postseptal fat stranding
key_facts: Several months of epiphora without prior dacryocystitis
Left-sided lacrimal sac abscess on CT
Postseptal fat stranding largely limited to the extraconal space
Acute injury to the entire orbital segment of the left optic nerve on diffusion-weighted imaging
Initial cultures isolated gram-positive cocci in chains, later identified as pan-susceptible Streptococcus pyogenes

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with left orbital pain, edematous and hyperemic left eyelids, diffuse limitation in extraocular movements, and imaging findings of a left-sided lacrimal sac abscess with postseptal fat stranding are consistent with orbital cellulitis. The presence of a lacrimal sac abscess and the isolation of Streptococcus pyogenes further support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: infections
rejected.why: Too broad, as the patient has a specific infection (Streptococcus pyogenes) causing a localized condition (orbital cellulitis).

rejected.label: visual impairment
rejected.why: A symptom rather than a diagnosis, as the patient's visual acuity is decreased (20/400 OS) due to the underlying condition (orbital cellulitis).

rejected.label: relative afferent pupillary defect
rejected.why: Not mentioned in the case, and the patient's symptoms and findings are more consistent with orbital cellulitis than a condition primarily affecting the pupil.

rejected.label: optic neuritis
rejected.why: Although the patient has acute injury to the orbital segment of the left optic nerve, the clinical presentation and imaging findings are more consistent with orbital cellulitis causing secondary optic nerve injury rather than primary optic neuritis.
